verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. ET (0007 GMT April 11).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Floating in the Pacific Ocean... off San Diego... After splashdown, at 8:07 p.m. Eastern time'; R2: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean, about 40 to 50 miles off the coast of San Diego... 8:07 p.m. ET'; R3: 'splashdown around 8:07 p.m... off the coast of San Diego... Friday, April 10'; R4: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on April 10, 2026... 8:07 p.m. EDT (0007 GMT April 11)'
verifications.reasoning: All references directly confirm exact location, date, and time of splashdown.

verifications.claim: The splashdown marked the safe return of four astronauts from a 10-day lunar mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'four astronauts... Their last day in space... after 10 days'; R2: 'four Artemis II astronauts back on Earth after their historic 10-day trip to the moon'; R4: '10-day test flight around the moon'; R5: 'four astronauts... nearly 10-day mission around the Moon'; R6: 'four astronauts... 10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references explicitly state safe return of four astronauts after ~10-day lunar mission.

verifications.claim: The landing occurred at approximately 20 mph after re-entering the atmosphere at 24,000 mph.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'hitting the waters at about 20 miles per hour... slipped into Earth’s atmosphere at more than 24,000 miles per hour... peak velocity of 24,664 miles per hour'; R2: 'safe velocity of less than 20 mph... top speed of about 24,000 mph'; R5: 'slowed the vessel to just 19 mph... speeds reaching 25,000 mph'
verifications.reasoning: References directly match speeds for reentry (~24,000 mph) and splashdown (~20 mph).

verifications.claim: The capsule carried astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch... Jeremy Hansen'; R2: 'Reid Wiseman... Victor Glover... Christina Koch... Jeremy Hansen'; identical in all references.
verifications.reasoning: All references list exactly these four astronauts aboard the capsule.

verifications.claim: The capsule underwent a "skip entry" maneuver to manage heat.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 're-entry trajectory was modified to reduce the heating'; R4: 'lofted entry sequence'; R6: 'dip into the atmosphere, then pop up again — like a stone skipping on the water’s surface'; R7: 'skip entry where we've shortened the duration of the skip'
verifications.reasoning: References describe modified 'skip' or 'lofted' entry to reduce heat exposure, directly supporting claim.

verifications.claim: Parachutes deployed to slow the craft to roughly 20 mph for a splashdown.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'main parachutes... final descent to the ocean, hitting the waters at about 20 miles per hour'; R2: 'Parachutes have begun to deploy to slow... less than 20 mph'; R3: 'deploy its drogue parachutes... three main parachutes... slow the capsule for splashdown'
verifications.reasoning: All references confirm parachutes slowed capsule to ~20 mph for splashdown.

verifications.claim: The crew was retrieved by the USS John P. Murtha using helicopters for extraction.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'U.S.S. John P. Murtha... hovering helicopters to take them to the U.S.S. John P. Murtha'; R2: 'flown to the flight deck of USS John P. Murtha... hoisted into waiting helicopters'; R3: 'flown to the USS John P. Murtha. Recovery teams will retrieve the crew using helicopters'
verifications.reasoning: References consistently describe recovery by USS John P. Murtha via helicopters.

verifications.claim: Artemis II was the first crewed lunar mission since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first people to leave low-Earth orbit since 1972'; R5: 'NASA’s first crewed lunar mission in more than 50 years'; R6: 'first crewed lunar mission in more than 53 years'
verifications.reasoning: References explicitly state first crewed mission beyond LEO/to moon since 1972/Apollo era.
